title.zh: 卷401 列傳一百八十八 向荣 和春 张国梁
title.en: Volume 401 Biographies 188: Xiang Rong, He Chun, Zhang Guoliang
title.raw: 卷401 列傳一百八十八 向荣 和春 张国梁

sentences.zh: 列傳一百八十八向榮，字欣然，四川大寧人，寄籍甘肅固原。

translations.literal: Biography 188: Xiang Rong, courtesy name Xinran, a native of Daning in Sichuan, with registered domicile at Guyuan in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Biography 188: Xiang Rong, courtesy name Xinran, was from Daning in Sichuan but registered as a resident of Guyuan in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 以行伍隸提標，為提督楊遇春所識拔。

translations.literal: He entered service as a common soldier under the provincial commander-in-chief's banner and was recognized and promoted by the provincial military commander Yang Yuchun.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a rank-and-file soldier in the provincial commander's establishment and was spotted and advanced by Yang Yuchun, the provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 從征滑縣、青海、回疆，常為選鋒。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns in Huaxian, Qinghai, and the Muslim borderlands, and was often chosen as a vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in Huaxian, Qinghai, and the Muslim frontier, regularly serving in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 積功擢至甘肅鎮羌營游擊。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was promoted to battalion commander of the Zhenqiang Garrison in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Merit in the field eventually raised him to battalion commander of the Zhenqiang Garrison in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，直隸總督琦善知其才，調司教練，累遷開州協副將。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of the Daoguang reign, Zhili Governor-General Qishan, knowing his talent, transferred him to oversee training and repeatedly promoted him to deputy commander of the Kaizhou garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1833, Zhili Governor-General Qishan, impressed by his ability, put him in charge of drill and steadily promoted him to deputy commander of the Kaizhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 海疆戒嚴，率兵駐防山海關。

translations.literal: When the coast was placed on alert, he led troops to garrison Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: When the maritime frontier was put on war footing, he took troops to hold Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 擢正定鎮總兵，調通永鎮。

translations.literal: He was promoted to brigade commander of Zhengding Garrison and transferred to the Tongyong garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was made brigade commander at Zhengding and then transferred to the Tongyong garrison.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，擢四川提督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was promoted to provincial military commander of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of the reign he was appointed provincial military commander of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，調湖南，平李沅發之亂，調固原。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to Hunan, pacified the rebellion of Li Yuanfa, and was then transferred to Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was sent to Hunan, put down Li Yuanfa's revolt, and afterward was reassigned to Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 廣西匪起，巡撫鄭祖琛不能制。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Guangxi, and Governor Zheng Zuchen could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out in Guangxi, Governor Zheng Zuchen proved unable to bring it under control.

sentences.zh: 榮於舊將中最負時望，文宗特調為廣西提督，倚以辦賊。

translations.literal: Among veteran generals Rong enjoyed the greatest contemporary reputation; Emperor Wenzong specially transferred him to be Guangxi provincial military commander and relied on him to deal with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong stood highest among the old commanders in public esteem, and Emperor Wenzong specially appointed him Guangxi provincial military commander, counting on him to handle the rebels.

sentences.zh: 是秋至軍，由柳州、慶遠進剿，以達宜山、象州，連破賊於索潭墟、八旺、陶鄧墟、猶山等處，賊氛稍戢。

translations.literal: That autumn he reached the army, advanced from Liuzhou and Qingyuan to suppress the rebels, reaching Yishan and Xiangzhou, and repeatedly defeated the rebels at Suotanxu, Bawang, Taodengxu, Youshan, and other places, so that rebel activity subsided somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the army that autumn and drove forward from Liuzhou and Qingyuan toward Yishan and Xiangzhou, winning a string of victories at Suotanxu, Bawang, Taodengxu, Youshan, and elsewhere until rebel activity eased.

sentences.zh: 惟洪秀全等踞桂平金田，狡悍為諸賊冠。

translations.literal: Only Hong Xiuquan and others held Jintian in Guiping, the most cunning and fierce among all the rebel bands.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hong Xiuquan and his followers, entrenched at Jintian in Guiping, remained the craftiest and most formidable of the rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 榮移兵往剿，賊以大黃江、牛排嶺為犄角。

translations.literal: Rong shifted his troops to suppress them; the rebels used Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge as flanking positions.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong moved his forces against them, while the rebels held Dahuang River and Niupai Ridge as paired strongpoints.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年春，攻大黃江，賊分出誘戰，率總兵李能臣、周鳳岐合擊，大破之，殲千數百人，賜號霍欽巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of the Xianfeng reign he attacked Dahuang River; the rebels sent out a detachment to lure him into battle, but he led brigade commanders Li Nengchen and Zhou Fengqi in a combined assault, inflicted a great defeat, and killed several thousand men, for which he was granted the title Huoqin Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1851 he assaulted Dahuang River. When the rebels tried to draw him off with a feint, he led brigade commanders Li Nengchen and Zhou Fengqi in a joint attack that routed them and killed several thousand men, earning him the Manchu title Huoqin Baturu.

sentences.zh: 水陸合攻牛排嶺，搗其巢，又追擊於新墟、紫金山，賊乃竄踞武宣東鄉。

translations.literal: Land and river forces jointly attacked Niupai Ridge and destroyed their nest; he pursued them again at Xinxu and Zijin Mountain, and the rebels then fled to occupy Dongxiang in Wuxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Combined land and river columns stormed Niupai Ridge and smashed their base, then pursued them through Xinxu and Zijin Mountain until the rebels bolted for Dongxiang in Wuxuan.

sentences.zh: 時周天爵為巡撫，與榮同勦賊，議不合，數戰未得利，廣州副都統烏蘭泰率兵來會。

translations.literal: At the time Zhou Tianjue was governor; he and Rong jointly suppressed the rebels, but their plans did not agree and several battles brought no success, until the deputy lieutenant-general of Guangzhou, Ulangtai, led troops to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhou Tianjue was then campaigning alongside Xiang Rong, but the two could not agree on strategy and several engagements went badly until Ulangtai, deputy lieutenant-general at Guangzhou, arrived with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊突圍竄象州。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the rebels broke out of encirclement and fled to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the rebels broke through the siege lines and fled toward Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮被譴，褫花翎，降三級留任，天爵亦罷軍事。

translations.literal: Rong was reprimanded, stripped of his peacock feather, demoted three ranks while retained in office, and Tianjue was also removed from military command.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong was censured, stripped of his peacock feather, demoted three ranks but kept on duty, and Zhou Tianjue was relieved of military command as well.

sentences.zh: 大學士賽尚阿代李星沅督師，命榮與烏蘭泰節制鎮將以下，迭詔戒榮同心協力，以贖前愆。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Saishanga replaced Li Xingyuan in overall command of the army and ordered Rong and Ulangtai to direct all brigade commanders and below; repeated edicts admonished Rong to work in concert and redeem his earlier fault.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Saishanga took over command from Li Xingyuan and put Xiang Rong and Ulangtai in charge of all field officers down to brigade commander; edict after edict urged Rong to cooperate fully and atone for his earlier failure.

sentences.zh: 賊踞象州中坪，其要路東曰桐木，西曰羅秀，榮與烏蘭泰分扼之。

translations.literal: The rebels held Zhongping in Xiangzhou; the key routes east were called Tongmu and west Luoxiu, and Rong and Ulangtai divided forces to block them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Zhongping in Xiangzhou, with the vital eastern route at Tongmu and the western at Luoxiu; Xiang Rong and Ulangtai split their forces to seal both approaches.

sentences.zh: 六月，榮由桐木進兵，偕烏蘭泰合剿，迭敗賊於馬鞍山及架村、黃瓜嶺、西安村，遂回竄桂平新墟、紫金山，恃險負嵎。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Rong advanced from Tongmu and, together with Ulangtai in joint suppression, repeatedly defeated the rebels at Ma'anshan and at Jiacun, Huanggualing, and Xi'ancun; the rebels then fled back to Xinxu and Zijin Mountain in Guiping, relying on rugged terrain to resist stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he advanced from Tongmu and, fighting alongside Ulangtai, routed the rebels again and again at Ma'anshan, Jiacun, Huanggualing, and Xi'ancun until they fell back on Xinxu and Zijin Mountain in Guiping, where steep ground let them dig in.

sentences.zh: 榮偕烏蘭泰等迭奪豬仔峽、雙髻山要隘，進破風門坳。

translations.literal: Rong, together with Ulangtai and others, repeatedly seized the strategic passes at Zhuzai Gorge and Shuangji Mountain and advanced to break Fengmen'ao.
translations.idiomatic: Working with Ulangtai and others, Xiang Rong took the key passes at Zhuzai Gorge and Shuangji Mountain in succession and then broke through Fengmen'ao.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊冒雨竄逸，官軍失利於官村，遂陷永安州，坐褫職留營。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the rebels slipped away in the rain; government troops were defeated at Guancun, and Yong'an Prefecture then fell; he was punished by dismissal from office while retained in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the rebels broke out in a rainstorm; government forces lost at Guancun and Yong'an Prefecture fell, for which he was stripped of rank but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 十一月，合攻永安，獲勝，復原官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they jointly attacked Yong'an, won victory, and he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month a combined assault on Yong'an succeeded, and his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 初，榮所部湖南兵，因榮子繼雄用事，軍心不服，故武宣、象州之役戰不力，皆歸咎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, among the Hunan troops under Rong's command, because Rong's son Jixiong wielded power, the troops were discontented; therefore in the campaigns at Wuxuan and Xiangzhou they fought without vigor, and all blame was laid on this.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Hunan troops under his command had fought half-heartedly at Wuxuan and Xiangzhou because his son Jixiong meddled in affairs and the men resented it, and everyone blamed that for the poor showing.

sentences.zh: 文宗排眾議，仍加倚任，而調四川兵以易湖南兵。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong set aside popular opinion and continued to rely on him heavily, but transferred in Sichuan troops to replace the Hunan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong overrode the critics and continued to trust him, though he replaced the Hunan contingent with troops from Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿不知兵，專倚榮與烏蘭泰。

translations.literal: Saishanga knew nothing of warfare and relied exclusively on Rong and Ulangtai.
translations.idiomatic: Saishanga knew nothing of war and leaned entirely on Xiang Rong and Ulangtai.

sentences.zh: 二人復不協，圍永安久不下。

translations.literal: The two men again did not cooperate, and the siege of Yong'an dragged on without success.
translations.idiomatic: The two men again fell out with each other, and the siege of Yong'an dragged on without result.

sentences.zh: 榮建議缺北隅勿攻，伺賊逸擊之。

translations.literal: Rong proposed leaving the northern corner unassailed and waiting to strike when the rebels broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong advised leaving the northern side open and ambushing the rebels when they tried to break out.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，天大雨，賊由北突出，迳犯桂林。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year there was heavy rain; the rebels broke out to the north and marched straight against Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year a downpour gave the rebels their chance: they burst out to the north and marched straight on Guilin.

sentences.zh: 榮由間道馳援，先賊至，賊冒榮旗幟襲城，擊走之。

translations.literal: Rong hurried relief by a side road and reached the city before the rebels; the rebels disguised themselves under Rong's banners to assault the city, but he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong took a side road to Guilin and arrived before the rebels, who tried to enter under his banners; he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 偕巡撫鄒鳴鶴急治守具，屢出奇兵擊賊城下，俘斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Together with Governor Zou Minghe he urgently prepared defenses, repeatedly sent surprise forces to strike the rebels below the walls, and captured or killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: With Governor Zou Minghe he rushed the city's defenses into order and again and again sent sorties against the rebels below the walls, taking or killing large numbers.

sentences.zh: 經月餘，援軍集，賊乃解圍北竄。

translations.literal: After more than a month relief armies gathered, and the rebels then lifted the siege and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month reinforcements arrived, and the rebels broke off the siege and fled north.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其保城功，已奪職復之，予議敘。

translations.literal: An edict praised his merit in preserving the city; his dismissed office was restored and he was granted consideration for reward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended him for saving the city, restored the rank he had lost, and ordered his merits recorded for reward.

sentences.zh: 賊由興安、全州入湖南。

translations.literal: The rebels entered Hunan by way of Xing'an and Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pushed into Hunan through Xing'an and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 榮頓兵桂林，為總督徐廣縉論劾，褫職戍新疆。

translations.literal: Rong halted his troops at Guilin and was impeached in memorial by Governor-General Xu Guangjin; he was stripped of office and banished to garrison duty in Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: While his army lingered at Guilin, Governor-General Xu Guangjin memorialized against him; he was stripped of rank and sent to serve in exile in Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿疏請暫緩發遣，令援湖南。

translations.literal: Saishanga memorialized asking that his dispatch be temporarily postponed and that he be ordered to relieve Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Saishanga asked that the exile order be held back for the moment and that Xiang Rong be sent to reinforce Hunan instead.

sentences.zh: 九月，至長沙，破賊瀏陽門外，又破之於見家河、漁網洲、岳麓山。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he reached Changsha, defeated the rebels outside the Liuyang Gate, and defeated them again at Jianjia River, Yuwangzhou, and Yuelu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Changsha, routed the rebels outside the Liuyang Gate, and won again at Jianjia River, Yuwangzhou, and Yuelu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 至冬，圍乃解。

translations.literal: By winter the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: By winter the siege had been raised.

sentences.zh: 賊北竄，陷岳州，入湖北，進犯漢陽、武昌，官軍遙尾之，莫敢擊。

translations.literal: The rebels fled north, took Yuezhou, entered Hubei, and advanced against Hanyang and Wuchang; government troops followed at a distance and none dared attack.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled north, seized Yuezhou, entered Hubei, and pressed on Hanyang and Wuchang while government columns trailed far behind and none dared close with them.

sentences.zh: 賽尚阿、徐廣縉先後罷黜，諸將無一能軍。

translations.literal: Saishanga and Xu Guangjin were dismissed one after another, and among the generals not one could command an army.
translations.idiomatic: Saishanga and Xu Guangjin were removed in turn, and none of the generals in the field could hold an army together.

sentences.zh: 詔以榮屢保危城，緩急尚欲恃之，予提督銜，幫辦軍務，責援武昌。

translations.literal: An edict stated that because Rong had repeatedly preserved cities in peril, in urgency the court still wished to rely on him; he was given the rank of provincial military commander, appointed to assist in military affairs, and charged to relieve Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The court noted that he had repeatedly saved cities on the brink and still wanted him in a crisis: he was given provincial military commander's rank, made an assistant in military affairs, and ordered to relieve Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 尋复授廣西提督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed Guangxi provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was again appointed provincial military commander of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 榮至，數奏捷，而武昌尋陷，褫職，仍留軍。

translations.literal: When Rong arrived he reported several victories, but Wuchang soon fell; he was stripped of office yet remained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he reported victory after victory, yet Wuchang soon fell; he lost his rank again but stayed with the army.

sentences.zh: 調署湖北提督，未幾實授，命為欽差大臣，專辦軍務。

translations.literal: He was transferred to act as Hubei provincial military commander, and before long was appointed in full; he was named Imperial Commissioner with sole charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to act as Hubei provincial military commander, confirmed in the post shortly after, and named Imperial Commissioner with sole charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 賊既踞武昌，勢益熾，不可復制矣。

translations.literal: Once the rebels held Wuchang their power grew ever fiercer and could no longer be brought back under control.
translations.idiomatic: With Wuchang in rebel hands their momentum became unstoppable.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，大舉東犯，連舟蔽江，棄城而去。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year they launched a great eastern offensive; boats lined the river bank to bank, and they abandoned the city and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year they marched east in force, their fleet covering the river from bank to bank, and abandoned the city as they went.

sentences.zh: 榮以克復聞，詔促躡追。

translations.literal: Rong reported recovery of the city; an edict urged him to press close in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong reported the city recovered, and an edict ordered him to press the pursuit hard.

sentences.zh: 榮所部兵多疲弱，遣撤六千餘名，料簡精銳，率總兵和春、李瑞、秦定三、玉山、福興沿江躡賊；

translations.literal: Most of the troops under Rong were weak and worn; he sent away more than six thousand men, selected the elite, and led brigade commanders He Chun, Li Rui, Qin Dingsan, Yushan, and Fuxing along the river in pursuit of the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Most of his troops were exhausted; he sent away more than six thousand men, kept the best, and with brigade commanders He Chun, Li Rui, Qin Dingsan, Yushan, and Fuxing pressed down the river after the rebels;

sentences.zh: 令提督蘇布通阿率川兵，總兵晉德布率滇兵來會。

translations.literal: he ordered provincial military commander Subutong'a to lead Sichuan troops and brigade commander Jindebu to lead Yunnan troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered Subutong'a with Sichuan troops and Jindebu with Yunnan troops to join him.

sentences.zh: 至九江，無舟，留半月，賊已掠安慶，陷江寧，為久踞計。

translations.literal: At Jiujiang there were no boats, and he remained half a month; the rebels had already raided Anqing and taken Jiangning, planning a long occupation.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiujiang he found no boats and was held up half a month while the rebels sacked Anqing, seized Jiangning, and settled in for a long stay.

sentences.zh: 榮至江寧，屯孝陵衛。

translations.literal: Rong reached Jiangning and encamped at Xiaolingwei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong reached Jiangning and encamped at Xiaolingwei.

sentences.zh: 時鎮江、揚州皆為賊踞，詔琦善剿江北，榮剿江南，分任軍事。

translations.literal: At the time Zhenjiang and Yangzhou were both held by rebels; an edict ordered Qishan to suppress the rebels north of the river and Rong those south of the river, dividing military responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang and Yangzhou were both in rebel hands; Qishan was ordered to handle the north bank and Xiang Rong the south, splitting command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 榮所部一萬七千餘人，攻通濟門外及七橋甕賊壘，連破之，進屯紫金山，結營十八座，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Rong's force of more than seventeen thousand men attacked rebel fortifications outside the Tongji Gate and at Qiqiaoweng, broke them in succession, advanced to encamp on Zijin Mountain, established eighteen camps, and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: His seventeen thousand-odd men stormed the rebel works outside the Tongji Gate and at Qiqiaoweng, took them one after another, moved up onto Zijin Mountain, pitched eighteen camps, and earned a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 江寧城內士民謀結合內應，屢爽期，迄無成功。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners within Jiangning city plotted coordinated action from within, but repeatedly missed the appointed times and never succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and townspeople inside Jiangning plotted an uprising in concert with the besiegers, but meeting after meeting fell through and nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 賊已分股由安徽北擾河南，而鎮江、揚州南北互應，大江上下游賊勢相首尾。

translations.literal: The rebels had already sent detachments north from Anhui to harass Henan, while Zhenjiang and Yangzhou responded to each other across north and south; up and down the Great River rebel strength linked head to tail.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel columns were already raiding north from Anhui into Henan, while Zhenjiang and Yangzhou coordinated across the river and rebel power up and down the Yangtze linked into one chain.

sentences.zh: 榮遣提督鄧紹良率兵八千規鎮江，總兵和春以舟師伺便夾擊，屢戰，進壁城下。

translations.literal: Rong sent provincial military commander Deng Shaoliang with eight thousand men to threaten Zhenjiang, while brigade commander He Chun with the river fleet waited for an opportunity to strike from both sides; they fought repeatedly and advanced to entrench below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong sent Deng Shaoliang with eight thousand men against Zhenjiang while He Chun's fleet waited to strike from the river; after repeated clashes they pushed their lines to the foot of the walls.

sentences.zh: 六月，紹良軍為賊所襲，退守丹徒鎮，榮令和春往援，遂代領其軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Shaoliang's army was attacked by rebels and fell back to defend Dantu Town; Rong ordered He Chun to go to his relief and then took command of his army in his place.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Deng Shaoliang's force was hit by the rebels and pulled back to Dantu; Xiang Rong sent He Chun to reinforce him and then took over his command.

sentences.zh: 賊注意蘇、常諸郡，以和春軍相持不得進，乃欲取道東壩。

translations.literal: The rebels turned their attention to the prefectures of Suzhou and Changzhou; blocked by He Chun's army and unable to advance, they then wished to take the route through Dongba.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fixed on the Suzhou and Changzhou region; checked by He Chun's force and unable to advance, they tried to move through Dongba instead.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊船入蕪湖，陷高淳，遣兵擊走之，令鄧紹良駐防。

translations.literal: In the tenth month rebel boats entered Wuhu and took Gaochun; he sent troops to drive them off and ordered Deng Shaoliang to garrison the place.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month rebel vessels entered Wuhu and seized Gaochun; he sent troops to drive them off and left Deng Shaoliang to hold the area.

sentences.zh: 既而皖北賊熾，和春赴援，榮請以提督餘萬清代督鎮江軍。

translations.literal: Before long rebel strength flared in northern Anhui and He Chun went to relieve it; Rong requested that provincial military commander Yu Wanqing act in his place to command the Zhenjiang army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel activity then surged in northern Anhui and He Chun went to help; Xiang Rong asked that Yu Wanqing take over command at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，賊犯東壩，遣副將傅振邦等協剿，賊退高淳，進復其城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year rebels attacked Dongba; he sent deputy generals Fu Zhenbang and others to assist in suppression; the rebels fell back to Gaochun and he advanced to recover that city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year rebels struck Dongba; he sent Fu Zhenbang and other deputy generals against them, drove them back to Gaochun, and retook the city.

sentences.zh: 賊乘江寧大營空虛，大舉來撲，率諸軍拒之，擒偽丞相譚應桂，俘斬三千餘。

translations.literal: The rebels, taking advantage of the emptiness of the Jiangning great camp, came in force to attack; he led the armies to resist them, captured the false chancellor Tan Yinggui, and captured or killed more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting the thin garrison at the Jiangning headquarters, the rebels attacked in strength; he led the armies out, took the Taiping chancellor Tan Yinggui, and killed or captured more than three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 總兵葉長春、吳全美以水師克下關水柵砲台，殪偽燕王秦日綱，進扼三山，營江路上游。

translations.literal: Brigade commanders Ye Changchun and Wu Quanmei with the river fleet captured the water barrier batteries at Xiaguan, killed the false Prince of Yan Qin Rigang, advanced to block Sanshan, and encamped on the upper reaches of the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade commanders Ye Changchun and Wu Quanmei took the Xiaguan river batteries with the fleet, killed the Taiping Prince of Yan Qin Rigang, seized Sanshan, and camped on the upper river.

sentences.zh: 賊聚太平府，與江寧相應。

translations.literal: The rebels massed at Taiping Prefecture in mutual support with Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels concentrated at Taiping Prefecture in coordination with Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 張國樑連克賊壘，乘勝复太平，殲賊首韋得真等。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang captured rebel fortifications in succession, followed up victory to recover Taiping, and destroyed rebel leaders including Wei Dezhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang took rebel fort after fort, pressed the advantage to retake Taiping, and wiped out rebel leaders including Wei Dezhen.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊出營於上方橋，三路來撲，又撲七橋甕，分擊敗之，三戰殪賊二萬餘。

translations.literal: Jiangning rebels came out of camp at Shangfang Bridge and attacked in three columns; they attacked again at Qiqiaoweng; he divided his forces to strike and defeat them, and in three battles killed more than twenty thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels sallied from Jiangning at Shangfang Bridge in three columns and struck again at Qiqiaoweng; he split his forces, beat them back in three engagements, and killed more than twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 八月，毀上方橋賊壘，進逼雨花台，搗其巢，追奔至城下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he destroyed the rebel fortifications at Shangfang Bridge, advanced to press Yuhuatai, smashed their nest, and pursued the fleeing rebels to the foot of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he destroyed the works at Shangfang Bridge, pressed Yuhuatai, smashed their base, and chased the fugitives to the city wall.

sentences.zh: 賊復由觀音門出趨棲霞，令總兵德安追擊，敗之於高資汛，又與餘萬清合擊於夾江，擒斬殆盡。

translations.literal: The rebels again came out through Guanyin Gate toward Qixia; he ordered brigade commander De'an to pursue, defeated them at Gaozixun, and together with Yu Wanqing struck them jointly at Jiajiang and captured or killed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels sallied again through Guanyin Gate toward Qixia; he sent De'an in pursuit, routed them at Gaozixun, and with Yu Wanqing at Jiajiang killed or captured almost the entire force.

sentences.zh: 萬清亦屢敗賊於鎮江。

translations.literal: Wanqing also repeatedly defeated the rebels at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wanqing, too, won repeated victories over the rebels at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 五年春，湖北竄賊入蕪湖，鄧紹良御之於黃池。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year rebel bands from Hubei entered Wuhu; Deng Shaoliang met them at Huangchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year Hubei raiders entered Wuhu, and Deng Shaoliang met them at Huangchi.

sentences.zh: 瓜洲賊出鮎魚套犯高資，擊走之。

translations.literal: Rebels from Guazhou came out of Nianyutao to attack Gaozi; he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Guazhou came out of Nianyutao against Gaozi and were driven off.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊由蕪湖犯灣沚，卻之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month rebels from Wuhu attacked Wanzhi; he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month rebels from Wuhu struck Wanzhi and were turned back.

sentences.zh: 吳全美率水師破賊於東梁山，德安、明安泰率陸師進攻蕪湖，會鄧紹良大破安慶援賊，遂復蕪湖。

translations.literal: Wu Quanmei led the river fleet to defeat the rebels at Dongliang Mountain; De'an and Ming'antai led the land force to attack Wuhu; together with Deng Shaoliang they inflicted a great defeat on Anqing relief rebels and then recovered Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Quanmei routed the rebels at Dongliang Mountain by water while De'an and Ming'antai pressed Wuhu by land; with Deng Shaoliang they smashed the Anqing relief force and retook Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 餘賊猶濱江結壘，以廣福磯、弋磯為犄角，數路死力來援，紹良、全美等水陸苦戰，迭敗之而不能克也。

translations.literal: Remaining rebels still built fortifications along the river, using Guangfuji and Yiji as flanking positions; reinforcements came by several routes with desperate effort; Shaoliang, Quanmei, and others fought bitterly by land and water, repeatedly defeated them yet could not capture the positions.
translations.idiomatic: Surviving rebels still held riverbank forts with Guangfuji and Yiji as paired strongpoints; relief columns threw themselves into the fight again and again; Shaoliang, Quanmei, and the rest battled fiercely by land and water, beating the enemy repeatedly yet failing to take the forts.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫吉爾杭阿既克上海，詔幫辦軍務，專任鎮江一路，督攻甚急，江寧賊百計赴援。

translations.literal: At the time Governor Ji'erhang'a had already taken Shanghai and was ordered to assist in military affairs with sole charge of the Zhenjiang route; he pressed the attack urgently, and Jiangning rebels used every stratagem to send relief.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ji'erhang'a had taken Shanghai and was ordered to assist in military affairs with sole responsibility for the Zhenjiang front; he pressed the attack hard while the Jiangning rebels tried every means to send reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 十一月，榮督總兵德安、張國樑、秦如虎等，迭擊之於燕子磯、觀音門、甘家港、棲霞街、石埠橋等處，賊竄回江寧，令德安駐軍東陽鎮扼之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Rong directed brigade commanders De'an, Zhang Guoliang, Qin Ruhu, and others to strike them repeatedly at Yanziji, Guanyin Gate, Ganjiagang, Qixia Street, and Shipu Bridge; the rebels fled back to Jiangning, and he ordered De'an to garrison Dongyang Town to block them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Xiang Rong directed De'an, Zhang Guoliang, Qin Ruhu, and others in repeated blows at Yanziji, Guanyin Gate, Ganjiagang, Qixia Street, and Shipu Bridge until the rebels fled back to Jiangning; he left De'an at Dongyang Town to block them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，上游蕪湖、兩梁山、金柱關及江北瓜洲、金山、廬州、三河諸賊同趨江寧，約城中悍賊衝出：一由神策門至仙鶴門抄綴大營；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month rebels upstream at Wuhu, Liangliang Mountain, Jinzhuguan, and north of the river at Guazhou, Jinshan, Luzhou, and Sanhe all converged on Jiangning, coordinating with fierce rebels in the city to break out: one column from Shece Gate to Xianhe Gate to strike at the rear of the great camp;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month rebels from Wuhu, Liangliang Mountain, and Jinzhuguan upstream and from Guazhou, Jinshan, Luzhou, and Sanhe on the north bank all moved on Jiangning, timed with a sortie of the city's hard fighters: one column from Shece Gate toward Xianhe Gate to hit the great camp from behind;

sentences.zh: 一由觀音門沿江至棲霞，直趨鎮江；

translations.literal: one along the river from Guanyin Gate to Qixia, pressing straight on Zhenjiang;
translations.idiomatic: one down the river from Guanyin Gate to Qixia, driving straight for Zhenjiang;

sentences.zh: 一由南路秣陵關來犯。

translations.literal: one from the southern route through Muling Pass to attack.
translations.idiomatic: one from the south through Muling Pass.

sentences.zh: 榮令張國樑、秦如虎迎擊於仙鶴門，大捷，回擊石埠橋，賊亦退，又敗之於龍脖子及元山、板橋等處。

translations.literal: Rong ordered Zhang Guoliang and Qin Ruhu to meet the attack at Xianhe Gate with a great victory, then turned back to strike at Shipu Bridge and the rebels also retreated; he defeated them again at Longbozi and at Yuanshan, Banqiao, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong sent Zhang Guoliang and Qin Ruhu to meet them at Xianhe Gate and win a major victory, then swung back to Shipu Bridge and drove the rebels off again at Longbozi, Yuanshan, Banqiao, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 檄鄧紹良自蕪湖回援，餘萬清自鎮江移駐龍潭、下蜀街。

translations.literal: He summoned Deng Shaoliang from Wuhu to return in relief and shifted Yu Wanqing from Zhenjiang to garrison Longtan and Xiashu Street.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Deng Shaoliang from Wuhu and moved Yu Wanqing from Zhenjiang to hold Longtan and Xiashu Street.

sentences.zh: 六年春，賊踞倉頭，為往來要道，餘萬清、張國樑迭擊不退，鄧紹良至，令統前敵諸軍，屢戰不利。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year rebels held Cangtou, a vital thoroughfare; Yu Wanqing and Zhang Guoliang attacked repeatedly without driving them out; when Deng Shaoliang arrived, Rong put him in command of all front-line armies, but several battles went badly.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the rebels held Cangtou, a key crossroads; Yu Wanqing and Zhang Guoliang struck again and again without dislodging them; when Deng Shaoliang arrived Xiang Rong gave him the front-line armies, yet several fights went wrong.

sentences.zh: 賊日增多，蔓延炭渚、橋頭，改以張國樑為總統，國樑力戰，連破橋頭、下​​蜀街、三汊河、張楊村諸壘，賊始竄走，復合鎮江賊入瓜洲，將軍托明阿軍潰，江北大震。

translations.literal: Rebels increased daily and spread through Tanzu and Qiaotou; Zhang Guoliang was made overall commander; Guoliang fought fiercely and in succession broke the forts at Qiaotou, Xiashu Street, San Cha River, and Zhangyang Village; the rebels then fled, rejoined the Zhenjiang rebels to enter Guazhou, General Tuoming'a's army collapsed, and the north bank was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel numbers grew daily and spread through Tanzu and Qiaotou; Zhang Guoliang was made overall commander and fought hard, taking Qiaotou, Xiashu Street, San Cha River, and Zhangyang Village in turn until the rebels broke away, linked up with the Zhenjiang force, and entered Guazhou while General Tuoming'a's army collapsed and the north bank was thrown into uproar.

sentences.zh: 榮令紹良援揚州，偕德興阿復其城。

translations.literal: Rong ordered Shaoliang to relieve Yangzhou and, together with Dexing'a, recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong sent Shaoliang to Yangzhou, where with Dexing'a he retook the city.

sentences.zh: 國梁援六合，進克江浦、浦口，江北稍定。

translations.literal: Guoliang relieved Liuhe, advanced to take Jiangpu and Pukou, and the north bank was somewhat stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang relieved Liuhe, took Jiangpu and Pukou, and the north bank eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 四月，寧國告陷，蘇、浙戒嚴，令紹良馳御之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Ningguo reported fallen; Suzhou and Zhejiang were placed on alert, and he ordered Shaoliang to hurry to defend them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month word came that Ningguo had fallen; Suzhou and Zhejiang went on alert and he sent Shaoliang posthaste to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 江長貴亦退守黃池，而鎮江軍事复急。

translations.literal: Jiang Changgui also fell back to defend Huangchi, while military affairs at Zhenjiang again grew urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Changgui, too, pulled back to Huangchi, and the Zhenjiang front flared up again.

sentences.zh: 國樑進攻小丹陽未下，吉爾杭阿戰歿於煙墩山，鎮江京峴山營壘皆失，榮令餘萬清代領其軍。

translations.literal: Guoliang attacked Xiaodanyang without taking it; Ji'erhang'a was killed in battle at Yundun Mountain; the camps at Jingxian Mountain in Zhenjiang were all lost; Rong ordered Yu Wanqing to take command of his army.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang besieged Xiaodanyang without success; Ji'erhang'a fell at Yundun Mountain; the Jingxian Mountain camps at Zhenjiang were lost; Xiang Rong put Yu Wanqing in command of what remained.

sentences.zh: 明安泰扼小丹陽，福興、張國樑率兵防剿，以固蘇、常門戶。

translations.literal: Ming'antai blocked Xiaodanyang while Fuxing and Zhang Guoliang led troops in defense and suppression to secure the gateway to Suzhou and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ming'antai held Xiaodanyang while Fuxing and Zhang Guoliang guarded the approaches to keep Suzhou and Changzhou safe.

sentences.zh: 國樑破賊於丹徒鎮，進扼馬陵，而賊已陷溧水，由高資、下蜀街趨江寧，分屯太平、神策門外。

translations.literal: Guoliang defeated the rebels at Dantu Town and advanced to block Maling, but the rebels had already taken Lishui and, by way of Gaozi and Xiashu Street, pressed on Jiangning, dividing forces to encamp outside Taiping and Shece Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang beat the rebels at Dantu and moved to hold Maling, but they had already taken Lishui and, coming by Gaozi and Xiashu Street toward Jiangning, split their force between Taiping and outside Shece Gate.

sentences.zh: 五月，上游賊麕至，屯城北。

translations.literal: In the fifth month upstream rebels gathered in crowds and encamped north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month upstream rebels poured in and camped north of the city.

sentences.zh: 榮大營兵僅數千，急促國樑回援。

translations.literal: Rong's great camp had only a few thousand men; he urgently summoned Guoliang back to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: The great camp had only a few thousand men left; Xiang Rong urgently called Guoliang back.

sentences.zh: 賊分十餘路來撲，營壘盡失，退守淳化鎮，再退丹陽，自請治罪，詔原之，褫職，仍留欽差大臣，督辦軍務。

translations.literal: Rebels attacked in more than ten columns; all camps were lost; he fell back to defend Chunhua Town, then retreated again to Danyang; he asked to be punished, an edict pardoned him, stripped his office, yet retained him as Imperial Commissioner supervising military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hit in more than ten columns; every camp was lost; he fell back to Chunhua Town, then to Danyang; he asked to be punished, was pardoned but stripped of rank, and kept on as Imperial Commissioner in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 丹陽當鎮江、江寧兩路要衝，榮率張國樑、虎嵩林扼守。

translations.literal: Danyang stood at the vital junction of the Zhenjiang and Jiangning routes; Rong led Zhang Guoliang and Hu Songlin to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Danyang guarded the junction of the Zhenjiang and Jiangning roads; Xiang Rong held it with Zhang Guoliang and Hu Songlin.

sentences.zh: 令西林防句容，明安泰攻溧水，江長貴扼溧陽，張國樑仍總統諸軍。

translations.literal: He ordered Xilin to defend Jurong, Ming'antai to attack Lishui, Jiang Changgui to block Liyang, and Zhang Guoliang remained overall commander of the armies.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xilin to Jurong, Ming'antai against Lishui, and Jiang Changgui to hold Liyang, with Zhang Guoliang still overall commander.

sentences.zh: 賊更番至，恃國樑力禦卻之。

translations.literal: Rebels came in rotating waves; he relied on Guoliang's strength to hold them off and drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels came in wave after wave and were beaten back only by Guoliang's fighting.

sentences.zh: 疏請增兵，未至，榮憂憤成病，七月，卒於軍。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting reinforcements, but they had not arrived when worry and indignation brought on illness; in the seventh month he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for reinforcements in a memorial, but they never came; grief and anger wore him down, and in the seventh month he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 遺疏上，文宗震悼，詔嘉其忠勤，雖未恢復堅城，數年保障蘇、常，盡心竭力，復原官，依例賜卹，予一等輕車都尉世職，諡忠武。

translations.literal: His final memorial was submitted; Emperor Wenzong was deeply shaken and grieved; an edict praised his loyalty and diligence: although he had not recovered the fortified city, for several years he had guarded Suzhou and Changzhou, exhausting heart and strength; his former office was restored, condolence grants were made according to precedent, he was given the hereditary rank of first-class commandant of light chariots, and posthumously titled Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial reached the throne, Emperor Wenzong mourned him deeply and praised his loyal service: he had never retaken the walled city, yet for years he had shielded Suzhou and Changzhou with everything he had; his rank was restored, the usual mourning grants were made, his descendants received the hereditary rank of first-class commandant of light chariots, and he was posthumously titled Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 命建專祠，又入祀江蘇名宦祠。

translations.literal: He was ordered to have a special shrine built and was also entered for worship in the shrine of renowned officials of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered a special shrine built for him and enrolled him in the Jiangsu shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 克復江寧後，賜祭一壇，入昭忠祠。

translations.literal: After the recovery of Jiangning, one altar of sacrifice was granted and he was entered in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangning was retaken, the court granted a sacrificial altar and admitted him to the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 子繼雄，候選道，襲世職。

translations.literal: His son Jixiong, a candidate for the circuit intendant rank, inherited the hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jixiong, a candidate circuit intendant, inherited the hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 和春，字雨亭，赫舍里氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: He Chun, courtesy name Yuting, of the Heseri clan, a Bannerman of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun, courtesy name Yuting, of the Heseri clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 由前鋒、藍翎長授整儀尉，累遷副護軍參領。

translations.literal: From vanguard and chief of the blue plume he was appointed orderly officer of the guard, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commandant of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the vanguard and chief of the blue plume to orderly officer of the guard and then to deputy commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 出為湖南提標中軍參將，擢永綏協副將。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as regimental colonel of the central army of the Hunan provincial commander's banner, and was promoted to deputy commander of the Yongshui garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as regimental colonel of the Hunan provincial commander's central force and promoted to deputy commander of the Yongshui garrison.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，從向榮赴廣西剿匪，戰武宣東鄉，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he followed Xiang Rong to Guangxi to suppress bandits, fought at Dongxiang in Wuxuan, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he followed Xiang Rong to Guangxi against the rebels, fought at Dongxiang in Wuxuan, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 破賊於中坪，進攻紫金山，奪雙髻山、豬仔峽要隘，功最，賜號鏗色巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He defeated rebels at Zhongping, advanced to attack Zijin Mountain, seized the strategic passes at Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge with the greatest merit, and was granted the title Kengse Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the rebels at Zhongping, stormed Zijin Mountain, and took the key passes at Shuangji Mountain and Zhuzai Gorge—the top credit of the campaign—and earned the title Kengse Baturu.

sentences.zh: 又奪風門坳，克古調村賊巢，擢綏靖鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He again took Fengmen'ao, captured the rebel nest at Gutiao Village, and was promoted to brigade commander of Suijing Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He took Fengmen'ao as well, destroyed the rebel base at Gutiao Village, and was made brigade commander at Suijing.

sentences.zh: 二年，援桂林，力戰解圍，加提督銜。

translations.literal: In the second year he relieved Guilin, fought fiercely to lift the siege, and was given the rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he relieved Guilin in hard fighting and was given provincial military commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 追賊至全州，敗之。

translations.literal: He pursued the rebels to Quanzhou and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels to Quanzhou and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊入湖南，迭戰於道州、桂陽，遂犯長沙，和春從向榮赴援，數出奇破賊。

translations.literal: The rebels entered Hunan and fought repeatedly at Daozhou and Guiyang, then attacked Changsha; He Chun followed Xiang Rong to relieve it and several times used surprise tactics to defeat the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels entered Hunan, fought at Daozhou and Guiyang, and then struck Changsha; He Chun went with Xiang Rong to relieve the city and again and again surprised the rebels with decisive victories.

sentences.zh: 賊去陷岳州，坐追剿遷延，褫職留軍。

translations.literal: The rebels departed and took Yuezhou; he was punished for delay in pursuit and suppression, stripped of office, yet retained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels left and seized Yuezhou; he was stripped of rank for slow pursuit but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 三年春，會攻武昌。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year they jointly attacked Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he joined the assault on Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 賊棄城東下，追至九江，遇賊，襲擊之。

translations.literal: The rebels abandoned the city and went east; he pursued to Jiujiang, encountered rebels, and raided them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels abandoned the city and fled east; he pursued to Jiujiang, met the rebel fleet, and attacked.

sentences.zh: 從向榮抵江寧，分軍攻通濟門外賊壘。

translations.literal: Following Xiang Rong he reached Jiangning and divided his army to attack rebel fortifications outside the Tongji Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xiang Rong to Jiangning and split his force to storm the rebel works outside the Tongji Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋偕總兵葉長春、吳全美等率舟師攻鎮江，破賊甘露寺下。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, together with brigade commanders Ye Changchun, Wu Quanmei, and others, he led the river fleet to attack Zhenjiang and defeated the rebels below Ganlu Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined brigade commanders Ye Changchun and Wu Quanmei in a river assault on Zhenjiang and routed the rebels below Ganlu Temple.

sentences.zh: 駐金山扼江路，又掠鮎魚套，擊敗賊船。

translations.literal: He encamped at Jinshan to block the river route, also raided Nianyutao, and defeated rebel boats.
translations.idiomatic: He held Jinshan to control the river, raided Nianyutao, and smashed the rebel vessels.

sentences.zh: 偕總兵瞿騰龍攻太平門，填壕逼城，殲賊甚眾。

translations.literal: Together with brigade commander Qu Tenglong he attacked the Taiping Gate, filled the moat to press the city, and destroyed a great many rebels.
translations.idiomatic: With Qu Tenglong he assaulted the Taiping Gate, filled the moat to press the walls, and killed rebels in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 六月，提督鄧紹良師潰於鎮江，詔和春署江南提督，率所部廣東、湖南兵馳援。

translations.literal: In the sixth month provincial military commander Deng Shaoliang's army collapsed at Zhenjiang; an edict appointed He Chun acting Jiangnan provincial military commander, and he led his Guangdong and Hunan troops in haste to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Deng Shaoliang's force collapsed at Zhenjiang; He Chun was made acting Jiangnan provincial military commander and rushed his Guangdong and Hunan troops to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 移軍丹徒鎮，進复京峴山舊壘。

translations.literal: He shifted his army to Dantu Town and advanced to recover the old camps at Jingxian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Dantu Town and retook the old camps on Jingxian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊數千來爭，殲戮殆盡。

translations.literal: Several thousand rebels came to contest the position and were nearly all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand rebels came to retake the ground and were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 賊銳稍挫，兩軍相持，蘇、常得無事。

translations.literal: Rebel vigor was somewhat blunted; the two armies faced each other, and Suzhou and Changzhou remained unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels' edge was blunted, the two sides settled into a stalemate, and Suzhou and Changzhou were spared.

sentences.zh: 尋實授提督。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed provincial military commander in full.
translations.idiomatic: He was confirmed shortly afterward as provincial military commander.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，安徽軍事急，命和春分兵移防滁州，遂進援廬州。

translations.literal: That winter military affairs in Anhui grew urgent; He Chun was ordered to divide his troops to shift defense to Chuzhou and then advance to relieve Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Anhui front collapsed; He Chun was told to detach troops for Chuzhou and then push on to relieve Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫江忠源困守危城，陝甘總督舒興阿率援軍至，不敢戰，忠源疏言和春忠勇可恃，請命總督援軍，詔允之，而所部僅千人，請舒興阿分兵，不聽。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Zhongyuan was besieged in a perilous city; Shaanxi-Gansu Governor-General Shuxing'a led relief troops but dared not fight; Zhongyuan memorialized that He Chun's loyalty and courage could be relied on and asked that the governor-general's relief army be placed under his command; an edict approved this, yet his own force had only a thousand men, and when he asked Shuxing'a to divide troops, the request was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Zhongyuan was trapped in a doomed city; Shuxing'a of Shaanxi-Gansu arrived with relief troops but would not fight; Zhongyuan wrote that He Chun was loyal and brave enough to trust and asked that Shuxing'a's men be put under him—the court agreed, but He Chun had only a thousand men and Shuxing'a refused to share any.

sentences.zh: 未幾，廬州陷，忠源殉。

translations.literal: Before long Luzhou fell and Zhongyuan died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Luzhou fell and Jiang Zhongyuan died defending it.

sentences.zh: 軍事專屬和春，福濟繼任巡撫，為之副。

translations.literal: Military affairs were placed solely under He Chun; Fu Ji succeeded as governor and served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Command passed entirely to He Chun, with Fu Ji as the new governor acting as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏言：「皖省軍情重大，兵勇雖有萬餘，多未經戰陣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized: 'The military situation in Anhui Province is grave; although there are more than ten thousand soldiers and braves, most have not seen battle.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he wrote: 'Anhui is in grave danger. We have more than ten thousand men, but most have never seen combat.'

sentences.zh: 請調鎮江舊部湖南兵，並撥金陵得力官兵三千，交總兵秦定三、鄭魁士率之來助剿。

translations.literal: He requested transfer of his old Hunan troops from Zhenjiang and allocation of three thousand effective officers and soldiers from Jinling, to be led by brigade commanders Qin Dingsan and Zheng Kuishi to assist in suppression.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for his old Hunan troops from Zhenjiang and three thousand seasoned men from Nanjing under Qin Dingsan and Zheng Kuishi to reinforce the campaign.

sentences.zh: 」時廬州屬縣皆陷，與安慶踞賊連絡一氣，城大賊眾，和春駐軍三里岡，屢率鄭魁士等進剿，賊抗拒不下。

translations.literal: At the time all subordinate counties of Luzhou had fallen and linked with the rebels holding Anqing; the city was large and the rebels numerous; He Chun encamped at Sanligang, repeatedly led Zheng Kuishi and others in advance to suppress, yet the rebels resisted and could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: By then every county around Luzhou had fallen and was linked with the rebels at Anqing. The city was large and strongly held. He Chun camped at Sanligang and led Zheng Kuishi and others in repeated assaults, but the rebels would not yield.

sentences.zh: 乃沿河築壘構橋，分三路更番攻擊。

translations.literal: He then built fortifications and bridges along the river and divided into three routes to attack in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: He built river forts and bridges and attacked in rotation along three routes.

sentences.zh: 夏，知州茅念劬率民團克六安，秦定三破賊於三連橋，進攻舒城。

translations.literal: In summer Prefect Mao Nianqu led militia to take Lu'an; Qin Dingsan defeated rebels at Sanlian Bridge and advanced to attack Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Prefect Mao Nianqu's militia retook Lu'an, Qin Dingsan beat the rebels at Sanlian Bridge, and the army pressed Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 賊由霍山撲六安，擊走之。

translations.literal: Rebels from Huoshan rushed at Lu'an; he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Huoshan struck Lu'an and were driven back.

sentences.zh: 扎筏載大砲轟廬州城，賊分出拒戰，迭敗之。

translations.literal: He lashed rafts to carry heavy cannon to bombard Luzhou city; the rebels sent detachments to resist and were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He floated rafts with heavy guns to shell Luzhou; rebel sorties were beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 別遣軍复英山、廬江，而和州、含山一路賊時窺伺，疏請飭袁甲三嚴防烏江，以斷賊援。

translations.literal: He separately sent armies to recover Yingshan and Lujiang, while rebels along the Hezhou and Hanshan route watched for openings; he memorialized requesting that Yuan Jiasan be ordered to guard Wujiang strictly to cut off rebel relief.
translations.idiomatic: Other columns retook Yingshan and Lujiang, while rebels along the Hezhou-Hanshan line probed for weakness; he asked that Yuan Jiasan hold Wujiang tight and sever rebel relief.

sentences.zh: 冬，臧紆青、劉玉豹由廬南規桐城，連奪大關等隘，逼城下，而紆青戰歿，玉豹退保六安，和春為賊牽制不能救。

translations.literal: In winter Zang Shuqing and Liu Yubao from southern Luzhou moved against Tongcheng, seized passes including Daguan in succession, and pressed below the walls; but Shuqing was killed in battle, Yubao fell back to defend Lu'an, and He Chun was pinned by rebels and could not relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zang Shuqing and Liu Yubao advanced on Tongcheng from the south, took pass after pass including Daguan, and reached the walls; Shuqing was killed, Yubao fell back to Lu'an, and He Chun was too tied down to help.

sentences.zh: 秦定三攻舒城，亦久不下，迭詔切責。

translations.literal: Qin Dingsan attacked Shucheng but also could not take it for a long time; repeated edicts sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Dingsan's siege of Shucheng dragged on as well, and edict after edict rebuked the delay.

sentences.zh: 初，和春專剿廬州，袁甲三扼臨淮，軍事多相關，而意不合。

translations.literal: Earlier He Chun had sole charge of suppressing Luzhou while Yuan Jiasan blocked Linhuai; military affairs were often interrelated, yet their views did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: At first He Chun focused on Luzhou while Yuan Jiasan held Linhuai; their fronts were linked, but the two men could not agree.

sentences.zh: 五年，偕福濟疏劾甲三，罷之，命和春遣員接統其軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, together with Fu Ji, he memorialized to impeach Jiasan; Jiasan was dismissed and He Chun was ordered to send an officer to take over his army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he and Fu Ji memorialized against Yuan Jiasan, who was removed, and He Chun was told to send an officer to take over his troops.

sentences.zh: 夏秋連擊敗援賊，督諸軍急攻廬州，至十月克之，城陷將兩年矣。

translations.literal: Through summer and autumn he repeatedly defeated relief rebels, supervised the armies in urgent attack on Luzhou, and by the tenth month captured it; the city had been fallen nearly two years.
translations.idiomatic: Through summer and autumn he smashed one relief column after another and pressed the siege until Luzhou fell in the tenth month—nearly two years after it was lost.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉和春功能補過，賜黃馬褂，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: An edict praised He Chun's merit as making up for faults, granted a yellow riding jacket, and gave the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised He Chun for redeeming his record, gave him a yellow riding jacket, and granted the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 六年，复舒城，大破賊於三河，克之，再复廬江。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he recovered Shucheng, inflicted a great defeat on rebels at Sanhe and took it, and again recovered Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he retook Shucheng, routed the rebels at Sanhe and took the town, and recovered Lujiang again.

sentences.zh: 會向榮卒於軍，命和春代為欽差大臣，督辦江南軍務。

translations.literal: When Xiang Rong died in camp, He Chun was ordered to replace him as Imperial Commissioner supervising Jiangnan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Rong died in camp, He Chun was named Imperial Commissioner to take charge of the Jiangnan war.

sentences.zh: 自向榮兵挫，退守丹陽，江寧賊益驕，內閧，自相殘殺，故榮歿後，張國樑等得以撫輯餘軍，規復東壩、高淳。

translations.literal: Since Xiang Rong's army had been defeated and fell back to defend Danyang, Jiangning rebels grew more arrogant, quarreled internally, and slaughtered one another; therefore after Rong's death Zhang Guoliang and others were able to rally the remaining army and plan recovery of Dongba and Gaochun.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang Rong's defeat and retreat to Danyang, the Nanjing rebels grew overconfident, quarreled among themselves, and turned on one another; so after his death Zhang Guoliang and the others could rally the remnants and aim at retaking Dongba and Gaochun.

sentences.zh: 和春至，餉械並絀，詔下各省接濟月餉四十萬兩，江蘇糧台不能時給，疏劾總督怡良、巡撫趙德轍，詔勉其和衷。

translations.literal: When He Chun arrived, pay and arms were both short; an edict ordered the provinces to supply four hundred thousand taels monthly, but the Jiangsu grain office could not deliver on time; he memorialized to impeach Governor-General Yiliang and Governor Zhao Dezhe; an edict urged them to work in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When He Chun arrived, pay and arms were both short. The court ordered four hundred thousand taels a month from the provinces, but the Jiangsu supply office could not keep pace; he impeached Governor-General Yiliang and Governor Zhao Dezhe, and the throne told them to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 溧水、句容為賊精銳所聚，力攻數月，七年夏，先後克之，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Lishui and Jurong were where rebel elites gathered; he attacked fiercely for months, and in the summer of the seventh year took them in succession; he was given the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Lishui and Jurong held the rebels' best troops; he hammered at them for months and took both in the summer of the seventh year, earning the rank of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 圍攻鎮江，賊數糾悍黨來援，督諸將迭破之。

translations.literal: Besieging Zhenjiang, rebels repeatedly gathered fierce bands to relieve it; he supervised the generals in defeating them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenjiang the rebels sent wave after wave of hard fighters; he directed his generals to beat each relief force back.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克鎮江，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he took Zhenjiang and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Zhenjiang fell, and he received the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 將軍德興阿督江北諸軍攻瓜洲，同日克復，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: General Dexing'a directed northern-bank armies to attack Guazhou; it was recovered the same day and military prestige rose greatly.
translations.idiomatic: General Dexing'a took Guazhou the same day on the north bank, and the army's prestige soared.

sentences.zh: 進攻江寧東北路，奪太平、神策兩門外賊壘。

translations.literal: He advanced against the northeastern route of Jiangning and seized rebel fortifications outside the Taiping and Shece gates.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on the northeastern approaches to Nanjing and took the rebel works outside the Taiping and Shece gates.

sentences.zh: 八年春，賊迭出城，力鬥卻之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year rebels came out of the city repeatedly; he fought fiercely and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighth year the rebels sallied again and again, and he fought them back each time.

sentences.zh: 合水陸諸​​軍克秣陵關，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Combined land and river forces took Muling Pass, and he was given the rank of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Land and river columns together took Muling Pass, and he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 又破賊三汊河，奪要隘，江寧之圍漸合。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at San Cha River, seized strategic points, and the encirclement of Jiangning gradually closed.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the rebels at San Cha River, took the key ground, and the ring around Nanjing slowly closed.

sentences.zh: 賊由皖南犯浙境，用以牽掣​​大軍。

translations.literal: Rebels from southern Anhui invaded Zhejiang territory to tie down the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from southern Anhui struck into Zhejiang to pin down his main force.

sentences.zh: 詔和春兼辦浙江軍務，先遣兵二千往援，命親往督師，以病未行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered He Chun also to handle Zhejiang military affairs; he first sent two thousand troops to relieve it and was ordered to go in person to direct the army, but illness prevented his going.
translations.idiomatic: The court told him to take on Zhejiang as well, sent two thousand men ahead, and ordered him to go in person, but illness kept him from leaving.

sentences.zh: 尋浙事緩，罷其行。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Zhejiang affairs eased and his journey was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhejiang crisis soon eased, and the trip was called off.

sentences.zh: 賊复沿江來援，擊走，築長圍困之。

translations.literal: Rebels again came along the river in relief; he drove them off and built a long encirclement to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels came down the river again he drove them off and threw a long siege line around the city.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊大舉出撲，張國樑破之城下。

translations.literal: In the seventh month rebels came out in force to attack; Zhang Guoliang defeated them below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels attacked in strength, and Zhang Guoliang routed them below the walls.

sentences.zh: 八月，陳玉成糾合捻匪犯江浦、浦口，德興阿兵潰，儀徵、揚州、六合先後陷。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Chen Yucheng gathered Nian bandits to attack Jiangpu and Pukou; Dexing'a's army collapsed, and Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Chen Yucheng joined Nian fighters against Jiangpu and Pukou; Dexing'a's army broke, and Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 和春遣馮子材渡江赴援，复失利。

translations.literal: He Chun sent Feng Zicai across the river to relieve them, but he again met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun sent Feng Zicai across the river, but that relief force failed too.

sentences.zh: 張國樑繼往，力戰，复揚州、儀徵。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang went next, fought fiercely, and recovered Yangzhou and Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang went next, fought hard, and retook Yangzhou and Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 九月，和春授江寧將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month He Chun was appointed Jiangning general.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month He Chun was made general of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 江寧賊乘間出撲，溧水亦陷，急調國樑回援。

translations.literal: Jiangning rebels seized an opening to attack; Lishui also fell, and Zhang Guoliang was urgently recalled to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing rebels struck when they saw a gap; Lishui fell too, and Zhang Guoliang was rushed back.

sentences.zh: 十月，复溧水，而上游賊犯黃池、灣沚，鄧紹良戰沒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Lishui was recovered, but upstream rebels attacked Huangchi and Wanzhi, and Deng Shaoliang was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Lishui was retaken, but upstream rebels hit Huangchi and Wanzhi, and Deng Shaoliang was killed.

sentences.zh: 九年春，招降捻首薛之元，獻江浦城，复約李世忠破賊，复浦口。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he induced the Nian leader Xue Zhiyuan to surrender and present Jiangpu city, and again arranged with Li Shizhong to defeat rebels and recover Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he won over the Nian leader Xue Zhiyuan, who handed over Jiangpu, and with Li Shizhong retook Pukou.

sentences.zh: 因劾德興阿縱寇狀，詔罷德興阿。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to impeach Dexing'a for allowing rebels to escape, and an edict dismissed Dexing'a.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Dexing'a for letting the rebels run loose, and the court removed him.

sentences.zh: 江北不復置帥，諸軍並歸和春節制。

translations.literal: The north bank no longer had a separate commander; all armies were placed under He Chun's control.
translations.idiomatic: The north bank no longer had its own commander; every force came under He Chun.

sentences.zh: 提督鄭魁士亦克灣沚、黃池，進規蕪湖，軍事轉利。

translations.literal: Provincial military commander Zheng Kuishi also took Wanzhi and Huangchi and advanced against Wuhu; military affairs turned favorable.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Kuishi retook Wanzhi and Huangchi and moved on Wuhu, and the tide began to turn.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「揆察現勢，先盡力於金陵一路，絕其根株，則枝葉自萎。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Considering the present situation, we should first exert all strength on the Jinling route, cut off the root, and the branches and leaves will wither of themselves.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'Given the present situation, we should throw everything at Nanjing first. Cut the root and the branches will wither on their own.'

sentences.zh: 欲破金陵，必先斷浦口。

translations.literal: To break Jinling, we must first cut off Pukou.'
translations.idiomatic: To take Nanjing we must first sever Pukou.'

sentences.zh: 請添募精銳萬人，由張國樑統率，一面力攻，一面進扎營壘，斷賊糧路，兼卻外援。

translations.literal: He requested recruitment of ten thousand elite troops to be commanded by Zhang Guoliang, attacking with force on one side while advancing to pitch camps on the other, cutting rebel grain routes and also repelling outside relief.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked to raise ten thousand picked troops under Zhang Guoliang to press the attack, build camps forward, cut the grain routes, and block outside help.'

sentences.zh: 臣當相度事機，剋期蕆功。

translations.literal: Your servant will gauge the opportunity and complete the task within a set time.'
translations.idiomatic: I will watch for the right moment and finish within the deadline I set.'

sentences.zh: 」詔允之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，陳玉成由六合犯揚州，分黨渡江窺秣陵關，欲抄大營後路，東壩、溧水皆告警。

translations.literal: That winter Chen Yucheng from Liuhe attacked Yangzhou, sent detachments across the river to spy on Muling Pass intending to strike at the rear of the great camp, and both Dongba and Lishui raised alarms.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Chen Yucheng struck Yangzhou from Liuhe, sent parties across the river toward Muling Pass to hit the great camp from behind, and alarms sounded at Dongba and Lishui.

sentences.zh: 尋大舉犯江浦，提督週天培死之，遂陷浦口。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he launched a major attack on Jiangpu; provincial military commander Zhou Tianpei died there, and Pukou then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he attacked Jiangpu in force; Zhou Tianpei was killed, and Pukou fell.

sentences.zh: 張國樑、馮子材援剿獲勝，揚州解嚴，浦口仍為賊踞。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang and Feng Zicai relieved and suppressed them with victory; Yangzhou was placed off alert, but Pukou remained in rebel hands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang and Feng Zicai won the relief fight and eased the crisis at Yangzhou, but Pukou stayed in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 十年春，國樑督水陸軍攻九洑洲，大捷，破其老巢。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year Guoliang directed land and river forces to attack Jiufuzhou, won a great victory, and destroyed their old nest.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year Zhang Guoliang took Jiufuzhou by land and water in a major victory that smashed the rebels' river stronghold.

sentences.zh: 九洑洲為江寧水陸咽喉，既得，已成合圍之勢，而賊復由皖南犯浙，遽陷杭州，蘇、常震動。

translations.literal: Jiufuzhou was the land-and-water throat of Jiangning; once taken, a closing encirclement had already formed, but rebels again invaded Zhejiang from southern Anhui, swiftly took Hangzhou, and Suzhou and Changzhou were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Jiufuzhou was Nanjing's river gateway; once it fell the siege ring was nearly complete, but rebels from southern Anhui swept into Zhejiang, seized Hangzhou overnight, and threw Suzhou and Changzhou into panic.

sentences.zh: 詔和春仍兼辦浙江軍務，先後分兵萬餘，提督張玉良總統赴援，甫至，賊即棄杭州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered He Chun again to handle Zhejiang military affairs; he successively detached more than ten thousand troops; provincial military commander Zhang Yuliang was made overall commander to relieve it; as soon as he arrived, the rebels abandoned Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court again put Zhejiang under He Chun, sent more than ten thousand men in stages, and made Zhang Yuliang overall commander; the rebels abandoned Hangzhou as soon as he arrived.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，由廣德分犯建平、東壩、溧陽，遂窺常州，急調張玉良回援，賊已分路迳趨江寧。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month they divided from Guangde to invade Jianping, Dongba, and Liyang, then spied on Changzhou; Zhang Yuliang was urgently recalled to relieve it, but the rebels had already split into routes and pressed straight on Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month they fanned out from Guangde against Jianping, Dongba, and Liyang and then eyed Changzhou; Zhang Yuliang was rushed back, but rebel columns were already driving straight for Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時賊酋陳玉成、李秀成、李侍賢、楊輔清，糾諸路眾十餘萬，力破長圍，城賊應之。

translations.literal: At the time rebel chiefs Chen Yucheng, Li Xiucheng, Li Shixian, and Yang Fuqing gathered more than a hundred thousand from all routes, broke the long encirclement by force, and rebels in the city responded.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng, Li Xiucheng, Li Shixian, and Yang Fuqing then mustered more than a hundred thousand men from every direction, smashed the siege lines, and the garrison sallied out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 大營軍心不固，惟恃張國樑力禦。

translations.literal: Morale in the great camp was unsteady; they relied only on Zhang Guoliang's strength to hold the enemy off.
translations.idiomatic: The great camp's morale was cracking, and only Zhang Guoliang's fighting held the line.

sentences.zh: 戰數晝夜，諸營同時火起。

translations.literal: After several days and nights of fighting, all camps burst into flame at once.
translations.idiomatic: After days of fighting every camp burst into flame at once.

sentences.zh: 總兵黃靖、馬登富、吳天爵陣亡，全軍大潰，退守鎮江。

translations.literal: Brigade commanders Huang Jing, Ma Dengfu, and Wu Tianjue fell in battle; the whole army collapsed in great defeat and fell back to defend Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Brigade commanders Huang Jing, Ma Dengfu, and Wu Tianjue were killed; the army broke completely and fell back on Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 和春坐褫職留軍。

translations.literal: He Chun was punished by dismissal from office while retained with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun was stripped of rank but kept with the army.

sentences.zh: 又退丹陽，賊踵至，張國樑死之。

translations.literal: He retreated again to Danyang; rebels followed close behind, and Zhang Guoliang died there.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back again to Danyang; the rebels pressed after him, and Zhang Guoliang was killed.

sentences.zh: 和春奪圍走常州，督兵迎敵，被重創，退至無錫，卒於軍。

translations.literal: He Chun broke out of encirclement and fled to Changzhou, directed troops to meet the enemy, was severely wounded, fell back to Wuxi, and died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun broke out toward Changzhou, tried to rally a defense, was badly wounded, fell back to Wuxi, and died in camp.

sentences.zh: 總督何桂清棄城走，常州、蘇州相繼陷。

translations.literal: Governor-General He Guiqing abandoned the city and fled; Changzhou and Suzhou fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General He Guiqing abandoned his post and fled; Changzhou and Suzhou fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 江南軍自向榮始任，凡曆七年，至是熸焉，蘇、浙遂糜爛。

translations.literal: The Jiangnan army, from the time Xiang Rong first took command, had lasted seven years in all; at this point it was extinguished, and Suzhou and Zhejiang were then laid waste.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangnan army Xiang Rong had built lasted seven years; with this collapse it was gone, and Suzhou and Zhejiang were left in ruins.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔念和春前功，雖兵機屢挫，尚能血戰捐軀，復原官，依例賜卹，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉，合前世職並為二等男爵，諡忠壯，附祀江寧昭忠祠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict recalled He Chun's earlier merit: although military fortune was repeatedly defeated, he could still fight bloodily and give his life; his former office was restored, condolence grants were made according to precedent, he was given commandant of cavalry together with commandant of the cloud cavalry, combined with previous hereditary offices into a second-class baron, posthumously titled Zhongzhuang, and attached for worship in the Jiangning Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the court honored his earlier service: though fortune had turned against him, he had fought to the death; his rank was restored, the usual mourning grants were made, his heirs received combined hereditary ranks as a second-class baron, he was posthumously titled Loyal and Robust, and he was enrolled in the Jiangning Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 子霍順武，候選參將，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Huo Shunwu, a candidate regimental colonel, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huo Shunwu, a candidate regimental colonel, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 張國樑，字殿臣，廣東高要人，初名嘉祥。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang, courtesy name Dianchen, a native of Gaoyao in Guangdong, originally named Jiaxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang, courtesy name Dianchen, was from Gaoyao in Guangdong and was originally named Jiaxiang.

sentences.zh: 少材武任俠，為裡豪所辱，毀其家，走山澤為盜，不妄殺。

translations.literal: In youth he was talented in martial arts and chivalrous; insulted by local bullies who destroyed his family, he fled to mountains and marshes to become a bandit and did not kill indiscriminately.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was skilled and hot-tempered; local bullies ruined his family, and he fled to the hills as an outlaw who killed sparingly.

sentences.zh: 流入越南，後歸鎮南關。

translations.literal: He drifted into Vietnam and later returned to Zhennan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He drifted into Vietnam and later came back to Zhennan Pass.

sentences.zh: 按察使勞崇光聞其名，招降，剿匪多得其力。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Lao Chongguang heard his name, induced him to surrender, and in suppressing bandits often gained his help.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Lao Chongguang heard of him, won him over, and relied on him heavily against local bandits.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，破劇賊顏品瑤，斬於陣，盡殲其黨。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Xianfeng reign he defeated the fierce bandit Yan Pinyao, beheaded him in battle, and destroyed his faction entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In 1851 he defeated the major bandit Yan Pinyao, killed him in battle, and wiped out his band.

sentences.zh: 積功擢守備，繼隸向榮軍。

translations.literal: Through accumulated merit he was promoted to garrison commander and afterward was attached to Xiang Rong's army.
translations.idiomatic: Merit raised him to garrison commander, and he then joined Xiang Rong's command.

sentences.zh: 二年，從解桂林圍，復全州、永興，擢都司。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed in relieving the siege of Guilin, recovered Quanzhou and Yongxing, and was promoted to battalion commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he helped lift the siege of Guilin, retook Quanzhou and Yongxing, and was made battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 赴援湖南，迭破賊於醴陵​​、益陽、湘陰。

translations.literal: He went to relieve Hunan and repeatedly defeated rebels at Liling, Yiyang, and Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to reinforce Hunan, he routed the rebels at Liling, Yiyang, and Xiangyin in succession.

sentences.zh: 援武昌，戰於洪山，皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: He relieved Wuchang and fought at Hongshan, always serving as the army's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He went to relieve Wuchang and fought at Hongshan, always in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 三年，至江寧，逼城而軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he reached Jiangning and encamped pressing the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he reached Nanjing and camped against the walls.

sentences.zh: 國樑屯七橋甕，攻鍾山賊壘，先登受傷，溫旨垂問，益感奮，遇艱險，一往直前。

translations.literal: Guoliang encamped at Qiqiaoweng and attacked rebel fortifications on Zhongshan; he was first to scale the wall and was wounded; a gracious edict inquired after him, and he was all the more stirred to fight; meeting hardship and danger, he pressed straight ahead.
translations.idiomatic: He held Qiqiaoweng and stormed the rebel works on Zhongshan; wounded while leading the climb, he was cheered by an imperial message and fought all the harder, plunging ahead through every danger.

sentences.zh: 擢湖南永州營游擊。

translations.literal: He was promoted to battalion commander of the Yongzhou Garrison in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made battalion commander of the Yongzhou Garrison in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 雨花台為近城要地，屢力攻，幾克之，賜號霍羅琦巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Yuhuatai was a key position near the city; he repeatedly attacked with force and nearly took it, and was granted the title Huoluoqi Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuhuatai, a key height near the city, he assaulted again and again and nearly took it, earning the title Huoluoqi Baturu.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，复太平。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he recovered Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he retook Taiping.

sentences.zh: 太平在江寧上游，賊踞之以通糧運。

translations.literal: Taiping lay upstream of Jiangning; rebels held it to keep grain transport open.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping lay upstream of Nanjing, and the rebels held it to keep their grain route open.

sentences.zh: 府城三面阻水，惟東路通陸。

translations.literal: The prefectural city was blocked by water on three sides; only the eastern route connected by land.
translations.idiomatic: Water blocked the city on three sides; only the east had a land route.

sentences.zh: 賊聚千艘結四壘，設防甚密。

translations.literal: Rebels gathered a thousand boats and formed four fortifications with very tight defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed a thousand boats in four fortified camps with tight defenses.

sentences.zh: 國樑分三隊進，設伏縱火，自率精銳四百人突賊營，一戰克之，時稱奇捷。

translations.literal: Guoliang advanced in three columns, set ambushes and set fires, and personally led four hundred elite troops in a rush on the rebel camp; one battle took it, and at the time it was called a marvel of swift victory.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced in three columns, laid ambushes and set fires, and led four hundred picked men in a charge that took the camp in one fight—a victory hailed as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 擢廣西三江協副將。

translations.literal: He was promoted to deputy commander of the Sanjiang garrison command in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made deputy commander of the Sanjiang garrison in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 又攻雨花台，平賊壘，毀砲台。

translations.literal: He again attacked Yuhuatai, leveled rebel fortifications, and destroyed batteries.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yuhuatai again, leveled the rebel works, and destroyed the batteries.

sentences.zh: 剿南路竄賊，追入秣陵關，殲戮殆盡。

translations.literal: He suppressed rebel bands fleeing on the southern route, pursued them into Muling Pass, and destroyed nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted southern raiders into Muling Pass and killed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢福建漳州鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to brigade commander of Zhangzhou Garrison in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made brigade commander at Zhangzhou in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 大軍急攻鎮江、瓜洲，江寧賊時出窺伺，江北賊亦乘隙進圖牽制。

translations.literal: The great army pressed urgent attacks on Zhenjiang and Guazhou; Jiangning rebels came out from time to time to spy and probe, and north-bank rebels also seized openings to advance and tie down government forces.
translations.idiomatic: While the main force hammered Zhenjiang and Guazhou, Nanjing rebels probed the siege lines and north-bank columns struck wherever they saw a gap.

sentences.zh: 國樑隨方截擊，奔命不遑。
