translations.literal: Guoliang intercepted them wherever they appeared, rushing about without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang raced from point to point to cut them off, never catching his breath.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊聚倉頭、炭渚、下蜀街，以斷鎮江、江寧之師。

translations.literal: In the sixth year rebels massed at Cangtou, Tanzu, and Xiashu Street to sever the armies at Zhenjiang and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the rebels concentrated at Cangtou, Tanzu, and Xiashu Street to cut the Zhenjiang and Nanjing armies apart.

sentences.zh: 國樑總統諸軍合擊，旬日之間，殺賊萬餘，賊不得逞，乃渡江犯瓜洲，江北諸軍皆潰，又陷江浦、浦口。

translations.literal: Guoliang as overall commander jointly struck them; within ten days he killed more than ten thousand rebels and the rebels could not prevail; they then crossed the river to attack Guazhou, all northern-bank armies collapsed, and Jiangpu and Pukou also fell.
translations.idiomatic: As overall commander he joined the armies in a ten-day battle that killed more than ten thousand rebels; when they could not break through, they crossed the river against Guazhou, the north-bank forces collapsed, and Jiangpu and Pukou fell.

sentences.zh: 國樑馳援，連破賊於毛許墩、葛塘，复江浦、浦口。

translations.literal: Guoliang hurried to relieve them, defeated rebels in succession at Maoxudun and Getang, and recovered Jiangpu and Pukou.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang rushed over, beat the rebels at Maoxudun and Getang, and retook Jiangpu and Pukou.

sentences.zh: 特詔嘉獎，加提督銜。

translations.literal: A special edict commended and rewarded him and gave him the rank of provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict praised him and gave him provincial military commander's rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，巡撫吉爾杭阿戰歿，鎮江告急，溧水被陷，國樑回軍克之，而賊數路趨江寧，夾攻大營。

translations.literal: Before long Governor Ji'erhang'a was killed in battle, Zhenjiang reported urgent peril, Lishui was taken, Guoliang turned his army back and recovered it, but rebels came toward Jiangning by several routes and attacked the great camp from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Governor Ji'erhang'a was killed, Zhenjiang called for help, and Lishui fell; Guoliang marched back and retook it, but rebel columns converged on Nanjing and hit the great camp from several sides.

sentences.zh: 向榮不能禦，急調國樑回援，血戰累日，左足被槍傷，偕榮退保丹陽。

translations.literal: Xiang Rong could not hold them off and urgently recalled Guoliang; after days of bloody fighting his left foot was wounded by gunfire, and together with Rong he fell back to defend Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong could not hold the line and called Guoliang back; after days of bloody fighting a bullet wounded his left foot, and he withdrew with Rong to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時大江南北諸軍，賊所尤畏者，惟國樑一人。

translations.literal: At the time among all armies north and south of the river, the one the rebels feared most was Guoliang alone.
translations.idiomatic: Among all the armies north and south of the Yangtze, the rebels feared no one more than Guoliang.

sentences.zh: 賊勢忽南忽北，多方肄我，皆牽制國樑之計，果為所敗。

translations.literal: Rebel strength shifted suddenly south and north and harassed government forces on many sides—all plans to tie down Guoliang—and they were indeed defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shifted south and north and harassed the government on every side—all schemes to pin down Guoliang—and he beat them every time.

sentences.zh: 榮既病，軍事一倚之。

translations.literal: Once Rong fell ill, military affairs relied entirely on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong fell ill, the whole campaign rested on him alone.

sentences.zh: 將軍福興與國樑不協，詔福興移軍江西，以國樑幫辦江南軍務。

translations.literal: General Fuxing did not cooperate with Guoliang; an edict moved Fuxing's army to Jiangxi and appointed Guoliang to assist in Jiangnan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: General Fuxing clashed with him, so Fuxing was sent to Jiangxi and Guoliang was made assistant in charge of the Jiangnan war.

sentences.zh: 賊屢至，皆挫之。

translations.literal: Rebels came repeatedly and he defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Every rebel attack was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 榮卒於軍，命和春代將，未至，國樑激勵將士，解金壇圍，復東壩、高淳，進攻句容。

translations.literal: Rong died in camp; He Chun was ordered to replace him as commander, but before he arrived Guoliang roused the troops, lifted the siege of Jintan, recovered Dongba and Gaochun, and advanced to attack Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: When Rong died, He Chun was named to replace him; before He Chun arrived, Guoliang rallied the troops, lifted the siege of Jintan, retook Dongba and Gaochun, and advanced on Jurong.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢湖南提督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Hunan provincial military commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made provincial military commander of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 克句容，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: He took Jurong and was granted a yellow riding jacket.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jurong and received a yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 督諸軍規复鎮江。

translations.literal: He supervised the armies in planning recovery of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the armies in the drive to retake Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 高資為鎮江、江寧要衝，兩路悍賊麕聚力爭，連營二十餘裡，國樑大破之，斬偽安王洪仁等，又連破之於龍潭，援賊盡殲。

translations.literal: Gaozi was the vital junction of Zhenjiang and Jiangning; fierce rebels from both routes gathered in crowds to contest it, encamping in a line of more than twenty li; Guoliang inflicted a great defeat, beheaded the false Prince of An Hong Ren and others, again defeated them at Longtan, and relief rebels were entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozi, the hinge between Zhenjiang and Nanjing, the rebels' best troops massed along twenty li of camps; Guoliang routed them, killed the Taiping Prince of An Hong Ren and others, smashed them again at Longtan, and wiped out the relief force.

sentences.zh: 鎮江糧盡援絕，遂克其城，城陷賊已歷五年。

translations.literal: Zhenjiang's grain was exhausted and relief cut off; he then took the city, which had been in rebel hands for five years.
translations.idiomatic: With grain gone and relief cut off, Zhenjiang fell—the city had been lost for five years.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，文宗大悅，詔嘉國樑謀勇超群，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: When victory was reported Emperor Wenzong was greatly pleased; an edict praised Guoliang's strategy and courage as surpassing the common run and granted the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The throne was delighted, praised his surpassing courage and counsel, and granted the hereditary rank of commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 於是偕和春進規江寧。

translations.literal: He then advanced with He Chun to plan against Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved with He Chun against Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 八年，克秣陵關，賜雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he took Muling Pass and was granted the double-eyed peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took Muling Pass and received the double-eyed peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 复薄江寧城下，自春徂夏，迭戰破賊。

translations.literal: He again pressed close below Jiangning city; from spring through summer he fought repeatedly and defeated rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Nanjing again from spring through summer, beating the rebels in fight after fight.

sentences.zh: 築長圍，至秋乃成。

translations.literal: He built a long encirclement, which was completed only by autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He built the long siege line, which was not complete until autumn.

sentences.zh: 皖賊大舉來援，江浦、浦口、儀徵、揚州、六合先後陷。

translations.literal: Anhui rebels came in force to relieve the city; Jiangpu, Pukou, Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui relief columns came in force, and Jiangpu, Pukou, Yizheng, Yangzhou, and Liuhe fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 國樑渡江援剿，复揚州、儀徵。

translations.literal: Guoliang crossed the river to relieve and suppress them and recovered Yangzhou and Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang crossed the river and retook Yangzhou and Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 調江南提督，晉三等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiangnan provincial military commander and advanced to third-class commandant of light chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Jiangnan provincial military commander and advanced to third-class commandant of light chariots.

sentences.zh: 然賊仍踵故智，國梁兵至則走，去則復來。

translations.literal: Yet rebels still followed their old trick: when Guoliang's troops arrived they fled, and when he left they returned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels still used their old trick: they fled when Guoliang came and returned when he left.

sentences.zh: 九年，提督週天培戰死江浦，國樑坐褫世職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year provincial military commander Zhou Tianpei died fighting at Jiangpu, and Guoliang was punished by forfeiture of his hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Zhou Tianpei was killed at Jiangpu, and Guoliang lost his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 十年，合水陸諸軍克九洑洲，沿江賊爭投款，約期攻上下兩關，招撫五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the tenth year combined land and river forces took Jiufuzhou; rebels along the river competed to surrender, fixed a date to attack the upper and lower passes, and more than five thousand were induced to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the combined fleet took Jiufuzhou; rebels along the river rushed to surrender, a date was set to take the upper and lower passes, and more than five thousand men came over.

sentences.zh: 軍中方謂堅城旦夕可下，而浙江告警，兵分益單，饋運不繼。

translations.literal: In the army they thought the fortified city would fall within days, but Zhejiang raised alarms, forces were divided ever thinner, and supply transport could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: The army thought the walled city would fall any day, but alarms from Zhejiang thinned the ranks further and supplies ran short.

sentences.zh: 和春用翼長王濬策，兵餉三分留一，約待克城後補給，士卒皆怨，國樑力諫不聽。

translations.literal: He Chun adopted the plan of wing commander Wang Jun to retain one-third of pay and rations, promising to make up arrears after the city was taken; the troops all resented it, and Guoliang remonstrated forcefully but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun followed wing commander Wang Jun's plan to hold back a third of pay and rations until the city fell; the men seethed, and Guoliang protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 閏三月，賊猝大至，四路受敵，大營不守，偕和春退丹陽。

translations.literal: In the intercalary third month rebels suddenly arrived in force; attacked on four sides, the great camp could not be held, and together with He Chun he retreated to Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary third month the rebels struck suddenly from four directions; the great camp collapsed, and he withdrew with He Chun to Danyang.

sentences.zh: 國樑以馮子材在鎮江未敗，進謀扼守。

translations.literal: Guoliang, because Feng Zicai at Zhenjiang had not yet been defeated, advanced a plan to hold a blocking position.
translations.idiomatic: Since Feng Zicai still held Zhenjiang, Guoliang urged a blocking defense.

sentences.zh: 尋率師援丹陽，遇賊城外，兵忽潰，策馬渡河，沒於水。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he led troops to relieve Danyang, met rebels outside the city, his army suddenly collapsed, he spurred his horse across the river, and was lost in the water.
translations.idiomatic: He soon led a relief column to Danyang, met the rebels outside the walls, saw his men break, spurred his horse into the river, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 事聞，文宗震悼，猶冀其不死，命軍中偵訪，不得。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported Emperor Wenzong was deeply shaken and grieved; he still hoped Guoliang was alive and ordered the army to search for him, but he could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned him deeply and still hoped he had survived; search parties were sent, but he was never found.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，乃下詔優恤，追贈太子太保，祀昭忠祠，諡忠武，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職。

translations.literal: After several months an edict of generous condolence was issued; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, entered in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, posthumously titled Zhongwu, and granted commandant of cavalry together with one commandant of the cloud cavalry as hereditary offices.
translations.idiomatic: Months later the court granted full honors: Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, enrollment in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, the posthumous title Loyal and Martial, and combined hereditary ranks of commandant of cavalry and commandant of the cloud cavalry.

sentences.zh: 國樑驍勇無敵，江南恃為長城。

translations.literal: Guoliang's fierce courage was without rival; Jiangnan relied on him as its great wall.
translations.idiomatic: None matched his fighting fury; Jiangnan treated him as its great wall.

sentences.zh: 其歿也，數郡遂淪陷。

translations.literal: At his death several prefectures then fell.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, whole prefectures fell in his wake.

sentences.zh: 士民哀思，私立廟祀。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners mourned him and privately built temples for his worship.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and townspeople mourned him and built private shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 傳述戰績，與古名將同稱，往往附會過實，然益見威烈入人之深。

translations.literal: Accounts of his battles placed him alongside ancient famous generals; they often attached embellishments beyond fact, yet this only shows how deeply his martial majesty entered people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Stories of his battles ranked him with the great generals of old; much was exaggerated, yet that only shows how deeply his fame had sunk in.

sentences.zh: 同治三年，江寧克復，偽忠王李秀成就擒，言賊中咸重國樑，禮葬於丹陽尹公橋塔下，乃得遺骸焉。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Tongzhi reign Jiangning was recovered and the false Prince of Loyalty Li Xiucheng was captured; he said that within the rebels all honored Guoliang and had buried him with ceremony below the pagoda at Yingong Bridge in Danyang, and thus his remains were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In 1864 Nanjing was retaken and Li Xiucheng, the Taiping Prince of Loyalty, was captured; he said the rebels had all honored Guoliang and buried him with ceremony below the pagoda at Yingong Bridge in Danyang, and so his body was recovered.

sentences.zh: 詔加給三等輕車都尉，合前世職並為一等男爵。

translations.literal: An edict added the rank of third-class commandant of light chariots, combining with previous hereditary offices into a first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: The court added third-class commandant of light chariots and combined his hereditary offices into a first-class baronage.

sentences.zh: 祀江寧忠義祠，復與向榮合建專祠。

translations.literal: He was worshipped in the Jiangning Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness, and again a special shrine was built jointly with Xiang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was enrolled in the Jiangning Shrine of Loyalty and Righteousness and given a joint special shrine with Xiang Rong.

sentences.zh: 子廕清，襲男爵。

translations.literal: His son Yin Qing inherited the baronage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin Qing inherited the baronage.

sentences.zh: 論曰：粵匪初起，向榮與諸帥不和，致無成功，援桂林、長沙，為時所稱，故文宗終用之。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When the Guangdong bandits first rose, Xiang Rong did not harmonize with the various commanders, so there was no success; yet in relieving Guilin and Changsha he won contemporary praise, and therefore Emperor Wenzong in the end employed him.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When the rebellion first broke out, Xiang Rong quarreled with the other commanders and won no decisive victory, yet his relief of Guilin and Changsha won acclaim, and Emperor Wenzong kept him in service.

sentences.zh: 其規江南也，近未破鎮江、瓜洲犄角之勢，遠未清長江上游，無以製賊死命，數年支拄，暫保吳疆，固昧遠猷，亦限兵力。

translations.literal: In his planning for Jiangnan, nearby he did not break the paired strongpoint strength of Zhenjiang and Guazhou, and far off he did not clear the upper Yangtze, so there was no means to seize the rebels' vital point; for several years he propped up the situation and temporarily preserved the Wu region—certainly lacking far-reaching strategy, yet also limited by military strength.
translations.idiomatic: His Jiangnan strategy never broke the Zhenjiang-Guazhou pair in the near term or cleared the upper Yangtze in the far term, so he could not strike at the rebels' throat; he propped up the Wu region for years through lack of vision as much as lack of troops.

sentences.zh: 和春繼克鎮江，又以援浙分兵，垂成之敗，禍更烈焉。

translations.literal: He Chun afterward took Zhenjiang, yet again divided forces to relieve Zhejiang; a defeat on the verge of success brought disaster all the fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: He Chun did retake Zhenjiang, but splitting forces for Zhejiang turned near-success into catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 張國樑一時健者，使盡其用，功不止此。

translations.literal: Zhang Guoliang was the sturdiest man of his day; had his talent been fully used, his achievement would not have stopped here.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guoliang was the finest fighter of his age; used to his full capacity, his achievement would have gone further.

sentences.zh: 善夫胡林翼之言曰：「未扼賊吭，江寧原難遽复。

translations.literal: How apt is Hu Linyi's saying: 'Without gripping the rebels' throat, Jiangning was originally hard to recover quickly.'
translations.idiomatic: Hu Linyi put it well: 'Without seizing the rebels' throat, Nanjing could not be retaken quickly.'

sentences.zh: 」觀湘軍之所以成功，與向榮、和春等之所以蹉跌，兵事固無幸焉者矣。

translations.literal: Observing why the Hunan army succeeded and why Xiang Rong, He Chun, and others stumbled, in military affairs there is indeed no room for luck alone.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the Hunan Army's success with the failures of Xiang Rong, He Chun, and their like shows that war offers no shortcuts to fortune.
